speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked	the Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (a) why are secondary schools directed not to take in transfer pupils whose PSLE scores do not meet their cut-off points; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider allowing schools with vacancies to effect these transfers on a case-by-case basis if the point difference is not significant.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The rules for school admissions and transfers must be transparent and objective, in order to be fair to all students.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In fact, we had received feedback in past years from some parents who were unhappy that our transfer process was not sufficiently fair and transparent.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Some have also pointed out that the transfer process could be improved.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our schools receive transfer appeals for a wide range of reasons, including good performance in CCAs, past connections to the school or proximity of home to the school.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Many of these appeals are from students who had applied for the school in the Secondary 1 Posting Exercise but did not manage to get a place because they did not meet the cut-off point of the school.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: However, unless there are special circumstances, allowing students who had not met the cut-off-point to transfer schools would mean that CCA, connections or proximity to the school will take precedence over the PSLE T-score.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This will not be entirely fair or transparent to the many students who have a similar or even higher PSLE T-score but had not been admitted in the Secondary 1 Posting Exercise.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Principal can then consider all such qualified appeals and make an appropriate decision after considering other relevant factors.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This new guideline for transfers after the Secondary 1 Posting Exercise is to ensure and assure parents and students that the system for appeals and transfers is transparent, objective and fair to all students.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: MOE appreciates the need for an appeals system, to help our students and their families cope with unforeseen circumstances.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We will continue to exercise flexibility for appeals while maintaining a fair and transparent system.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Ultimately, any appeals system will rest on the good judgement of experienced professionals, especially our school Principals.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Yes, I do receive many complaints from parents and, this time, it is about the sudden change in the policy or the announcement that no appeal will be entertained at all if they do not meet the minimum cut-off point of that particular school.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: My first clarification is: what is the timeframe given for the parents when they announce this?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I understand it was after they had made the choice for the schools, after the school listing is out.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I can understand there is a need for transparency.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I am very happy to hear that the Ministry will exercise flexibility.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The question is striking a balance between flexibility and transparency.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The Acting Minister mentioned that there were 800 appeals that were successful, and there were some that did not meet the cut-off point and, based on special circumstances, they were accepted into the schools.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Could the Acting Minister elaborate on the special circumstances for those who did not meet the cut-off point?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Lastly, will the Ministry consider giving the Principal or the School Advisory Committee (SAC) some form of flexibility to admit certain numbers of students, so that they have some autonomy rather than completely no appeals at all?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Some Principals were complaining to me that they had no choice because the Minister said that there are no appeals to be entertained.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For the first issue of complaints on the communications process, the Ministry, in implementing these new guidelines, could have done better in the communications.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We will take that as a lesson learnt and see how we can improve it this year.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For the circumstances of students who were transferred without meeting the cut-off point, let me give the Member one good example.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We acceded to an appeal from a student who had a birth defect, a spinal cord problem.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The student requires regular cleaning of the bladder, every four hours or so.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In the initial posting, she was posted to a school that was a little further away, by about 1 kilometre.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But upon appeal and seeing the circumstances, we facilitated a transfer to another school closer to her home, even though she did not meet the cut-off point.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We do exercise flexibility as such to ensure that the students' needs are appropriately taken care of.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So long as they have met the cut-off point, the flexibility was given fully to the Principals and schools.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: On the way ahead, we will see how we can work on some flexibility without undermining the Principals, as I have stated earlier.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We have a fine balance to maintain between the fairness of the system and some flexibility for appeals.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, it is a fair system and we will study how we can see some of the appeals that may require special attention.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This is because I came to learn about a lot of feedback from parents who were caught unawares about the change in policy and, because of that, they were quite upset.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The other clarification that I wish to ask the Acting Minister is: does that mean MOE is now going back to the situation where a student's PSLE score is the main factor in deciding where to go for a Secondary school?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Because I understand that, previously, MOE did say that PSLE score is not the main thing.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, right now, it seems that if you do not meet the cut-off point, that is it for you.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: You cannot go to a school of your choice.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, there is a good balance between academic emphasis and non-academic achievements.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Before PSLE, this exercise is carried through the DSA so that we can afford students to be admitted into the schools.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Once, however, the PSLE T-score comes out, it would be better, as we have said earlier, to maintain a system that is seen to be fair, transparent and meritocratic.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But overall, the system remains one that recognises different pathways for students to succeed.
